name: Agricultural Structures & Buildings

objectives.text: Identify common types of agricultural structures, such as barns, machine sheds, greenhouses, grain bins, and hoop buildings, and the purpose each serves on a farm
Identify the major components of an agricultural building, including the foundation, framing, siding, and roofing
Describe the ventilation, lighting, and drainage needs of a livestock housing structure and how each supports animal health
Compare wood, steel, concrete, and masonry as building materials for agricultural structures in terms of strength, durability, maintenance, and cost
Interpret a simple building plan to identify dimensions, materials, and construction details
Calculate board feet and distinguish nominal from actual dimensions when selecting lumber for a project
Explain how dead, live, snow, and wind loads travel through roof, wall, and foundation members of a farm building
Calculate a bill of materials and cost estimate for a small agricultural structure from a given plan
Explain the symbols, parts, and views used in plans for agricultural structures
Summarize the characteristics of an appropriate building site and complete a site analysis checklist to select a location for a farm structure
Examine building code requirements for agricultural structures and describe the role of the officials who enforce them
Develop a scaled, fully dimensioned plan of an agricultural structure by hand
Demonstrate procedures for assessing and preparing a building site, including setting batter boards and squaring a foundation layout
Calculate concrete volume for footings and slabs and demonstrate forming, placing, and finishing concrete
Calculate rafter lengths and cuts for a given roof pitch using a framing square or rafter tables
Construct an agricultural structure or structural component, such as a framed wall, small shed, or livestock shelter, from wood, metal, or masonry by following plans for an SAE or chapter project
Construct plans for agricultural structures using computer-aided design or drafting software
Analyze a client's needs to determine structural requirements, specifications, and a cost estimate for a proposed agricultural building
Analyze natural and mechanical ventilation options for a livestock barn or greenhouse based on air exchange, moisture, and temperature needs
Conduct a functionality and safety assessment of an existing agricultural structure using industry standards and local code
Develop a maintenance and repair plan for an agricultural building that identifies deterioration such as rot, corrosion, settling, and roof leaks and prioritizes corrective work
Design a functional agricultural building for a stated purpose using the design process, producing plans and a bill of materials and justifying material and layout choices against cost and use

changes: Kept all six original competencies, rewording a few, and split the grade 9 code and site objective into a site analysis objective (grade 9) and a building code objective (grade 10). Added structure types, materials comparison, lumber calculation, structural loads, plan symbols and views, scaled hand drafting, CAD plans, foundation site preparation, concrete work, rafter framing, hands-on construction tied to SAE and chapter projects, client needs analysis, ventilation analysis, safety and functionality assessment, and maintenance planning. Wiring, plumbing, and fencing content was left to sibling sub-topics. AFNR codes are attached only from grade 9 up where the objective directly teaches the standard. FPS.02.02.03.a was not used.
